source.title: From Flat to Hierarchical: Extracting Sparse Representations with Matching Pursuit
source.authors: Valérie Costa; Thomas Fel; E. Lubana; Bahareh Tolooshams; Demba E. Ba

record.tranche_reason: The study's own synthetic and pretrained-representation results refine the idea that sparse features must have globally quasi-orthogonal geometry: it reports hierarchy-dependent, conditionally orthogonal structure and cases where learned feature recovery degrades or trades off one kind of structure for another.
record.gate_note: The study reports feature-geometry results for synthetic hierarchical data and learned dictionaries, including dictionary and co-activation coherence. Those bear on V1's geometry component, but the synthetic ground truth has 20 concepts in R20, not more features than dimensions. It does not test the original toy-model superposition setup or establish its sparsity-dependent transition. Reconstruction, effective-rank, modality-score, and other results not measuring a version's named claim are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Mainly a method paper (MP-SAE), but on the same pretrained representations it shows that SAE encoder choice changes the extracted features. Standard SAEs give modality-split, globally quasi-orthogonal dictionaries; MP-SAE gives multimodal, globally coherent ones. This bears on V5's claim that SAE features are canonical units. The synthetic hierarchy is hand-generated (20 vectors in R20, not learned by any network and not overcomplete), so it tests SAE recovery, not V1's toy-model superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that standard SAEs work under the linear representation hypothesis but struggle with hierarchical, nonlinearly accessible and multimodal features. MP-SAE, built to favour conditional orthogonality, recovers such structure, which they take to show that purely linear, independently accessible features are an insufficient assumption. They note MP-SAE's bias may fit flat, entangled or categorical regimes poorly, and is greedy and possibly brittle under noise.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce Toy Models of Superposition. It trains and compares SAE architectures on a synthetic hierarchy and pretrained representations, using learned dictionaries, feature-recovery outcomes, and Babel coherence rather than the original toy-model intervention and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic feature recovery changes with ground-truth within-level correlation (0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9). At high correlation, MP-SAE prioritizes hierarchical organization over matching within-level correlation and uses greater support.

fits_no_version.finding: On a hand-built hierarchical generator, standard SAEs show feature absorption (Table 1 absorption ~0.45–0.70 for Vanilla/BatchTopK vs ~1e-3 to 7e-2 for MP-SAE). Matryoshka introduces negative sibling interference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Standard SAEs fail to recover known hierarchical (parent/child) features, absorbing children into parents.

record.problems: The synthetic ground truth has 20 concepts in R20, so it does not directly test the overcomplete more-features-than-dimensions superposition setting. Several reported geometry outcomes are qualitative descriptions of figures without numerical values; the text does not give uncertainty for those outcomes. The paper does not validate whether learned SAE features are the underlying canonical units of pretrained models.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested geometry results. Reconstruction, effective-rank, modality-score, and inference-time sparsity results were not extracted because they do not measure V1's feature-overlap geometry.

untested.parts: All. No network is trained to store more sparse features than dimensions; synthetic features are hand-placed (20 in R20). No sparsity transition or geometry of learned weights is measured.
All; no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity competition is measured.
Whether model features are spread across neurons; SAE recovery of true model features is not validated.
Completeness and seed stability of SAE features are not tested; only dependence on encoder architecture is tested.
All. The paper discusses nonlinear accessibility, not feature dimensionality.

missing.what: Modality score distributions: standard SAEs give bimodal image-only/text-only features; MP-SAE gives many multimodal features on the same embeddings.
missing.locator: Section 4.2 'Recovering Multimodal Concepts', Fig. 9; Appendix B.4, Fig. 19 (CLIP, SigLIP, SigLIP2, AIMv2)

missing.what: Pairwise D^T D histograms: standard SAE dictionaries sharply peaked at zero; MP-SAE broader with nonzero mass.
missing.locator: Appendix B.3, Fig. 17 (DINOv2, SigLIP, CLIP, ViT at k=5)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 labels are dropped. The synthetic benchmark measures SAE recovery of features the authors placed by hand, not superposition learned by a network, and it is not overcomplete. Rows r1–r16 are the study's own method versus baselines. The V5 verdict is limited: it shows architecture dependence of SAE features, not instability across seeds.

versions.untested_parts: Tests geometry of sparse feature representations in a synthetic hierarchy and learned dictionaries, but not the original overcomplete toy-model superposition setting (more features than dimensions), a sparsity-dependent superposition transition, or regular geometry across sparsity and importance.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity competition or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not measure polysemantic neurons or test whether they arise without capacity pressure.

The paper analyzes SAE codes and dictionary geometry, including a small language model, but does not test whether LLM features are spread across neurons or validate SAE recovery of underlying LLM features.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
Does not compare one-dimensional features against multidimensional features as the units of superposition; nonlinear sequential encoding is not itself a test of feature dimensionality.

rows.subject: MP-SAE
rows.size_stated: 20 ground-truth concepts in R20; SAE width not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared learned feature geometry and sparse-code recovery with the ground truth.
rows.measure: Recovery of hierarchy and within-level structure; inferred support
rows.baseline: Ground-truth hierarchy and sparsity of 1–2 active concepts
rows.value: Separates the hierarchy into four orthogonal sublevels of 1, 10, 3, and 6 features; preserves conditional structure but reduces within-level correlation and increases support, with most inputs activating 2–4 components.
rows.note: The paper describes a trade-off: hierarchy is maintained at the cost of matching the ground-truth correlation and sparsity.
rows.check: The study's own method's behaviour at 0.9 correlation; not V1.

rows.stage_stated: pretrained vision-model final-layer representations; ImageNet-1K SAE training
rows.operation_detail: Measured Babel coherence for full learned dictionaries.
rows.measure: Babel score, representing cumulative feature interference
rows.value: MP-SAE dictionaries have higher overall Babel scores than standard SAE dictionaries, indicating greater global interference.
rows.note: The text describes the comparison across tested models but gives no numerical scores.
rows.check: Not V1: Babel score measures SAE dictionary coherence, not how the vision model stores features. It bears on V5: the same representations yield globally quasi-orthogonal dictionaries (standard SAEs) or globally coherent ones (MP-SAE), so dictionary geometry depends on encoder choice.

relationships.condition: SAEs trained on the same pretrained vision, VLM and TinyStories representations with different encoders (ReLU/TopK/BatchTopK vs MP-SAE)
relationships.reason: Dictionary coherence (r17–r20) and modality selectivity of features (text, Fig. 9/19: split vs multimodal units) change with encoder choice, so SAE features are not method-independent units.
relationships.display_finding: On the same representations, dictionary coherence and whether features were split by modality or multimodal changed with the encoder, so SAE features were not method-independent units.
